I was not remotely ambivalent about what I wanted: to be free. That was the reason to make money."

His rise at Bear Stearns was a swift one. And he soon became the protégée of Jimmy Cayne (also hired by Ace Greenberg on a whim—he met him in a bridge game), who would go on to run Bear and to lose his fortune in Bear's 2006 collapse). Epstein's leave-taking or ouster from Bear was the result of politics, envy,
overreaching, or a securities violation, or...unclear. But, no matter, when he left in 1982 he took with him billionaire clients, including Marvin Davis, a real estate developer who owns Twentieth Century Fox, and Herb Seigel, a major media investor in the 1980s. At this point, Epstein was dating Morgan Fairchild, a television
star in the new mega-rich-family soap operas, Dallas and Falcon Crest.

The Concorde phase of his life coincided with the Concorde phase of the 1980s. If the '80s were happening pell mell in New York, they were happening at double time and catch up speed in London. Thirty-year-old Epstein was living a Lifestyle of the Rich and Famous (he befriended the show's star, Robin Leach), at
English shooting parties and country estates with Saturday night black tie dinners, where he was meeting the over-the-top families of Europe.
